summary: Make the existing Task-029 Linux reference sandbox launch portable across util-linux and BusyBox unshare implementations without changing its isolation semantics.

impacts.evidence: The portability correction changes only the namespace and chroot command spelling; sandbox sessions retain the existing host-created connector scope and introduce no tenant authority.
The probe still stages only the static emulator and returns the existing bounded isolation report; no persisted fields, provider payloads or credential material are added.
No public API, SDK surface or serialized operation result is changed by replacing util-linux-specific launcher options with portable equivalents.
The Linux reference probe emits no EventBus event and the patch does not alter any event envelope or event catalog entry.
Connector SDK v1 and the Task-025 admission plan remain unchanged; only the Task-029 host launcher invocation is made compatible with both supported unshare implementations.
The reference sandbox is transient and the portability fix adds no database schema, migration or stored runtime state.

The same user, mount, network, IPC and UTS namespaces, minimal chroot and fixed environment remain mandatory; the compatibility fix restores execution of that existing isolation proof in BusyBox images.
No operation authorization, approval policy, capability grant or production-credential rule is changed by the launcher portability correction.
Probe results retain the existing bounded usage and isolation evidence shape, with no new audit or lineage payload.
The change affects only deterministic test-process startup and cannot alter business retries, inbox, outbox or reconciliation behavior.

The namespace probe continues to require a network namespace with no direct route, while the portable invocation makes that existing direct-network isolation evidence executable in BusyBox-based qualification images.
Wall, CPU, RSS, output and concurrency ceilings and their measured result fields are unchanged.
Qualification operations gain compatibility with the pinned Alpine toolchain; rollback is a code-only revert and temporary chroot cleanup remains unchanged.
The external isolation probe now passes in a privileged pinned Alpine runtime and the full Task-064 reference conformance gate remains 13/13.
